new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Acrobat PDFMaker 2004, text present). extracted text gives, under the header 'Awiyaana and Kosena (Auyana, Awiyaana, Kosena) OPD Printed: August 16, 2004 Page 3', the section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' with exactly 'Stress is always on the first syllable.' followed by 'There are two phonemic tones, high [ ] and low [].' and the pairs aau'a 'canna' / aau'a 'wet season', toima 'mud' / toima 'type of tree'. The bracketed tone marks extract as U+F0DB and U+F0DD (Symbol-font glyphs), exactly as the compiler noted. No other stress/accent statement anywhere in the 4 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent over the whole extract finds only this section plus the bibliography entry…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog lists Auyana with an empty rule and no existing statement; this source supplies the placement (fixed initial) and adds that the language also has two phonemic tones marked independently of stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the first syllable of the word, with no stated exceptions. The language is at the same time tonal: two phonemic tones (high vs low) contrast on syllables, illustrated by minimal pairs whose high tone can sit on a non-initial syllable (aaú'a vs aáú'a, toimá vs toímá; also kumbá 'axe', tuvuó 'to kill', ontamá 'door' elsewhere in the sheet), so stress and high tone are independent of each other.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated ('always'). The sheet notes that /e/, /o/ and the low vowel can be lengthened, and the SPA/Bee note on non-contrastive penultimate lengthening is not repeated here.
new_statements.identity_note: Marks 1992 covers both dialects together, 'Awiyaana and Kosena (Auyana, Awíyááná, Kóséna) Language [AUY]', Awiyaana at Okapa and Kosena at Kainantu; the example words are marked 'from Kosena' and the stress statement is given for the language as a whole without dialect restriction. The 1974 grammar is specifically the Kosena dialect. The SPA 1979 'Auyana' sheet is actually Usarufa (usar1243) data and is not about this language.
